chunks: Indeed, this money is neither for me nor for you,
but it is the collective property of the Muslims and the acquisition of their swords,
If you had taken part with them in their fighting you would have a share equal to theirs,
otherwise the earning of their hands cannot be for other than their mouths.

key_terms.جَنَاةُ أَيْدِيهِمْ: The earning or gain of their hands
key_terms.فَيْءٌ: Collective property or spoils of war

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for distributing treasury wealth in Shia governance according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies to Abd al-Allah ibn Zama that the treasury (Bayt al-Mal) is not personal wealth but collective property acquired through military effort, establishing the principle of public trust. He links financial entitlement directly to participation in warfare, noting that those who do not fight share in the spoils only if they contribute to the collective effort, otherwise the reward for the fighters' labor remains exclusive to them. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly view of governance as a stewardship where fiscal rights are tied to communal sacrifice and military service.
